questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University, available courses, also somewhere in europe that differed culturally from Denmark

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I signed up for the Mentor program which helped a lot, and made check in to for example the dormitory i stayed in much easier, as not everyone who worked there spoke english

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared room in dormitory

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: shared kitchen was available

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: definitely worth to try, so nice to share your Exchange with a roommate, cheap housing and a fun way to meet people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: first come first serve - kind of process where we choose courses, got in or got on a waitlist, but also had the oppertuinity to write to teachers directly. a bit confusing

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: teachers and coordinators were helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very, as some were already full of full-time students or were cancelled, but i found others i enjoyed

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just because you end up on a waitlist, there is still a good chance you can get into the course if you talk to the respective teachers in person. there is a long drop inn/drop off period where this can work

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the levels of the courses and the expected work for each course was different, not really something that could be tied down to being either masters or bachelor lvl.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were generally smaller, which meant that there was more time for questions, better ability to speak and just more interaction with the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociological theories of populism 
European origins of zionism 
Introduction to history 
Czech republic in a nutshell 
Cultural studies: an introduction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i would recommend them all, as they we all interesting and gave a unique perspective, but i would especially recommend European origins of Zionism and Sociological theories of Populism. the teachers we very good and the topic also. generally very engaging classes

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had decided to say yes to everything, so i spent a lot on cultural activities, eating out, trips and travel.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fresh food, fruit and vegetables were more expensive than i had expected. CZ was also hit really hard by inflation in 2022, and that could still be seen sometimes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i didn't attend any activities hosted by CU, a bit through ESN which was fun

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i didn't attend any activities hosted by CU, only a bit through ESN which was fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Prague is nice and there is so many oppertunities always, but visiting other cities for day trips (Kutna Hora, Brno, Pilzen, Cesky Krumlov, Ceske budejovice etc) is so nice

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I did the intensive language course before the start of the semester which made all the difference, it made it so much easier to understand what was happening around me and find my place

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living in the dormitory made it easier to meet local students. i can also recommend signing up for the mentor program as you get to meet a czech student that can guide you a bit

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not a big challenge, but compared to Denmark, people are more vary of strangers in CZ

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: honesty, generally punctuality and no-bullshit

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do a language course in person, not just Duolingo
Stay in the dormitory
take the opportunity to travel around and see the country, as CZ is not just Prague, which can really be a bubble.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: expect different but very nice university at CU

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from different countries and cultures, sharing experiences and especially sharing the exchange together. i had it in my head that i would be going on exchange alone, and while thats true in theory, it is so nice to know that i shared it with a lot of other people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: going home again:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
